mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 2.5% in a given month coincides with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discount rates eroding expected equity payoffs.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 2.5% in the current month
failure_condition: Over 60-day rolling window, 20-day forward returns remain non-negative during high-rate months, or the FEDFUNDS shock is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly rise in UNRATE above 6.5% predicts a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return as higher labor market disengagement reduces consumer wealth and corporate hiring intentions.
regime_hint: High unemployment or weak wage growth
failure_condition: In regimes with low inflation and strong GDP growth, UNRATE spikes above 6.5% but 5-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When monthly GDPC1 (real private consumption) exceeds INDPRO by more than 5% in the same month, it indicates strong demand, which is associated with a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as firms anticipate higher sales.
regime_hint: Economic expansion with strong consumption relative to production
failure_condition: Over 12-month rolling window, this consumption-to-production gap persists but 60-day forward returns remain flat or negative (median p-value > 0.5).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive decline of at least 3% in INDPRO over two consecutive months signals supply-side weakness, leading to a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates slower corporate earnings.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by ≥3% in month t and again in month t+1
failure_condition: During periods of supply-side resilience (e.g., low inflation and rising capacity utilization), INDPRO declines by ≥3% consecutively but 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 4-month decline in CPIAUCSL below 237 (yearly chained 2017 dollars) indicates deflationary pressure, which is associated with a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as investors anticipate lower inflation and potential rate cuts.
failure_condition: Over 12 months, CPIAUCSL remains above 237 but 60-day forward returns during deflationary episodes are not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in PAYEMS (labor market activity) above the 12-month moving average while HOUST (hourly employment) remains flat suggests a labor market peak, which precedes a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return as profit expectations cool.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month moving average and HOUST unchanged
failure_condition: In regimes with robust GDP growth and low unemployment, this labor peak pattern occurs but 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly convergence of RSAFS (retail sales) and HOUST (employment) above 100% of their 12-month averages signals a dual-demand recovery, which is associated with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as consumer and labor confidence both improve.
regime_hint: Dual recovery in retail and labor markets
failure_condition: During periods of simultaneous supply shocks, this dual-demand signal appears but 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in FEDFUNDS below 1% for three consecutive months in a non-recessionary regime predicts a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return as markets anticipate tighter policy and lower growth expectations.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% for 3 consecutive months and RSI(FEDFUNDS) < 40
failure_condition: In recessionary regimes, FEDFUNDS falls below 1% for 3 months but 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05).
